device.description: 8-bit single-channel voltage-output DAC with I2C interface and power-down
device.note: dac5571.pdf (SLAS405A) p.1-2 pinout (SOT23-6 pin description), p.3 electrical characteristics (VDD 2.7-5.5 V, logic inputs), p.4-5 timing, p.15-16 I2C update sequence, address byte, CTRL/MSB and LSB bytes (Figure 45), p.17 power-on reset (zero code) and power-down modes (Table 1)

registers.name: DAC
registers.note: p.17: power-on fills the DAC register with zeros

registers.name: CTRL
registers.note: PD1/PD0 of the CTRL/MSB byte (Table 1): 0 normal, 1 1k to AGND, 2 100k to AGND, 3 Hi-Z

commands.name: Write CTRL/MSB + LSB
commands.note: Figure 45: 0 0 PD1 PD0 D7-D4, D3-D0 X X X X; n words per transaction; update at the ACK after the LSB byte

pages: p.1-2 (pinout), p.3 (VDD, logic levels), p.4-5 (I2C timing), p.15-16 (I2C protocol, data bytes), p.17 (power-on reset, power-down modes)
notModeled: analog output, settling and power-down output loads (PD bits stored only; the output is never driven)
broadcast address 1001000 (responds regardless of A0): not expressible in the address table
address pin A0 is latched at power-up (the model reads it live)
I2C high-speed mode master code and timing limits
the 0 0 bits of the CTRL/MSB byte: a byte with them nonzero is ignored rather than handled as the datasheet leaves undefined
variants: DAC5571 has its own datasheet (dac5571.pdf); DAC6571 (10-bit) and DAC7571 (12-bit) are the same family with wider data fields
